cards.question: Cell Two asked for the harvest count by Friday. Send it now?
cards.why: The steward is waiting on it to plan the gathering's table.
consequences: I will tell Cell Two the count is coming today.
I will tell Cell Two it waits until next week.
I will ask Cell Two who else can send it.

cards.question: You said you would write up the harvest notes by Tuesday. Is it on track?
cards.why: Tuesday is three days off, and Cell Two's steward is the witness.
consequences: I will keep Tuesday in view and remind you on Monday.
I will ask the steward whether Thursday works.
I will tell Cell Two it is free for someone else.

cards.question: The Commons asks who can help carry the long tables on Friday. Can you?
cards.why: The tables are a day late, and the gathering needs them.

cards.why: A branch across the lane is a danger to everyone who walks it.

deal.briefing: The harvest count Cell Two asked for is a day past, and the whole of Cell Two is waiting on the meeting day.

cards.question: The Commons asks to borrow your folding chairs for the winter market. Lend them?
cards.why: They are asked for by Monday, and you are not using them.
consequences: I will tell the Commons the chairs are theirs for the market.
I will tell the Commons not this time.
I will ask the Commons who else has chairs.

cards.question: Your agent finished the budget for the gathering. Read what it found?
cards.why: It asks for your yes before the steward sees it.
cards.unlocks: The steward's copy of the budget

cards.question: The Commons decided to hold the winter market on the first Saturday of December. Confirm it?
cards.why: What was decided is written, its conditions are met, and no one has spoken against it.

cards.question: A question for you: "May Cell Two light the evening fire in your garden?"
cards.why: It was asked of you as keeper of your home, and the gathering plans around it.

cards.question: Sort the seed packets now?
cards.why: It has room to wait until November.

proposals.text: Lay the long tables in the barn for the market.
Keep a soup pot going all day, free for anyone.
Run a seed swap at the barn door.
Ask each house to lend one folding chair.
String lanterns along the lane so the evening is safe.
Give the children a corner to make cards.
Set up a mending table for coats and tools.
Ask the fiddlers to play at noon.
Draw a map of the stalls for the gate.
